turns.sent: I want to build a small web app for my book club, 8 to 15 people. We pick a book, meet about once a month, and right now it's all in a group chat. Help me figure out the first version and what to build first.
turns.reply:
## The problem

You and 7 to 15 friends pick a book, meet about once a month, and coordinate in a group chat. I'm guessing at the specific pain because you didn't say: the important stuff gets buried. "What are we reading, when is it, whose place, who's coming?" scrolls away under memes, someone asks again, and a person (probably you) re-posts it. Picking the next book is worse. Suggestions come in over a week and nobody can tell what's winning.

## What I'd challenge

**The weakest assumption is that people will open a link instead of the chat.** The chat isn't going anywhere, and it already has polls and pinned messages. If the pinned message plus a chat poll would fix 80% of this, you don't need an app.

The cheap test happens to be the first slice itself. It's a weekend of work, so building it costs about as much as faking it. Ship the one-page version before the next meeting, post the link in the chat, and watch what happens.

## Success and stop signals

- **Working:** by the second meeting, most RSVPs come through the app and nobody asks "wait, when is it?" in the chat.
- **Stop:** after two meetings, fewer than half the members have used it and you're still re-posting the details in the chat. That means a pinned message was the answer all along.

## First version

One page: **the next meeting.**

1. You post a club link in the chat. Someone opens it on their phone.
2. The first visit asks "Who are you?" They tap their name from the member list, and it's remembered on that device.
3. They see the book (title, author, cover), the date and time, the place, and the host.
4. **The core action is RSVP:** Going, Maybe, or Can't make it. Their name shows up under their choice right away, so they know it saved.
5. You use a separate organizer link to set up the next meeting and manage the member list.

- **Empty state:** "No meeting scheduled yet." Members see that. Organizers also get a "Schedule the next one" button.
- **Error state:** if an RSVP fails to save, keep their choice selected, say it didn't save, and offer a retry. Don't silently reset it.
- Works on a phone and with a keyboard. The RSVP buttons are a real radio group, not clickable divs.

**Left out on purpose:** book voting (that's slice 2, and the next most valuable thing), accounts and passwords, email reminders, comments and discussion (the chat already does that), reading progress, ratings, past-book history, and AI recommendations.

## Requirements

- **Trust:** the people are friends, so a secret link is the login. Possession of the member link means you're in, and you choose your name. The catch is that anyone with the link can RSVP as anyone. For a book club that's fine. If the link leaks, you rotate it. The organizer link is a separate secret.
- **Personal data:** first names, plus the meeting place. If people host at home, that's **home addresses behind a shared link**. I'd keep the address off the page, show "Sam's place", and let the address stay in the chat. Or show it only to members and accept the risk. Your call, and it's the one privacy decision that matters here.
- **Data:** clubs, members, meetings, books, RSVPs. Small and relational. One RSVP per member per meeting, enforced by a unique constraint so a double tap can't create two.
- **Cost ceiling:** $0. Upkeep ceiling: near zero, since you won't babysit a book club app.

## Stack

- **Next.js on Vercel Hobby.** One app, one deploy, preview URLs. It's non-commercial, so Hobby fits.
- **Neon Postgres plus Drizzle.** The data is relational and the unique RSVP constraint does real work. Fifteen people checking once a month leaves the database asleep almost all the time, nowhere near the free compute cliff.
- **No auth library.** The secret links are a random token in the URL plus a cookie for "who I am". This is the call I'd defend hardest. Adding Better Auth means email sign-in, which means an email provider, which means a verified domain, all for 15 friends.
- **Book covers** come from a public book cover API by ISBN or title, stored as a URL. No file storage.
- **Tailwind plus shadcn/ui.** It should look like a nice little club page, not a framework default.

**What would make me add things:** strangers joining, or members actually impersonating each other, gets real auth. Missed meetings get email reminders, but try an "Add to calendar" (.ics) button first, which is nearly free. Running more than one club works with the schema as designed, so it needs no rewrite.

Prices come from SWE OS's stack recipe, checked Oct 6. I didn't re-check them, but at this scale every tier is free.

## Next step

Build slice 1, the next-meeting page with RSVP, and get the link into the chat before your next meeting. If you're in, I'll set up the repo with start-project and record these decisions in `PROJECT.md`.

Two questions first:

1. **What's actually the worst part today: logistics, or picking the next book?** If it's the book picking, I'd swap the order and build voting first.
2. **Do you meet at people's homes?** That decides whether addresses go on the page.

turns.reply:
The project is set up. `npm install && npm run dev` starts Postgres and the app with no Docker, and `npm run check` passes. The secret-scan hook is installed, but I couldn't confirm it blocks a secret, because running gitleaks needs approval I don't have.

**Set up.**
- **Next.js 16 (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind)**, scaffolded with `create-next-app`. It's your default stack.
- **Local Postgres from the `embedded-postgres` npm package.** It downloads real Postgres 18 binaries as an npm dependency, so there's nothing to install and no Docker. It also uses the same connection protocol as Neon, so moving to Neon later is just setting `DATABASE_URL`.
- **Drizzle and postgres.js.** The schema and migrations are written in TypeScript, and each migration is a SQL file you can review in `drizzle/`.
- **`npm run dev` is the one command.** It starts Postgres on port 54329, applies migrations, seeds four books on the first run, then starts Next. Ctrl+C stops both.
- **Tests run against their own Postgres.** Vitest starts a temporary database in a temp folder on a free port, so tests never touch your dev data and don't need the dev server running.
- **`check`** runs Prettier, ESLint, a typecheck, and Vitest. CI runs `check` and `build`, plus a gitleaks scan.
- **Pinned and protected:** `.nvmrc` pins Node 22, the lockfile is in the repo, `.env.example` lists the variables with no values, and `.env*` files are gitignored.

**Evidence.**
- **Dev server:** the home page streamed all four seeded books from Postgres. After I stopped it, no Postgres process was left running.
- **Build:** `npm run build` passed with no database running. The home page is built as a static shell, and the books load at request time.
- **Fresh copy:** I exported only the tracked files, then ran `npm ci && npm run check`. Formatting, lint and types passed, and both tests passed. The copy is deleted.
- **Secret scan:** not verified. Running gitleaks needs approval in this session. I staged a fake token, couldn't run the hook, then removed the file. To test it, put a fake `ghp_…` token in a file, `git add` it, and run `.githooks/pre-commit`; it should exit non-zero.

**For Tommy to do.**
- Run the secret-scan test above.
- I ran `git init` and staged everything, but didn't commit. Commit when you're happy with it.
- When it's on GitHub, connect it to [Vercel](https://vercel.com/new) for preview deploys. Add [Neon](https://neon.com/docs/guides/neon-managed-vercel-integration) when you first deploy.

**Deferred** (also in PROJECT.md):
- **The goal and first slice.** This folder was empty, and none of the earlier session's planning was saved, so PROJECT.md says the goal is unknown. The `books` table is a placeholder to prove the database works end to end. Tell me what we agreed on and I'll write it in, or change the table.
- **Production database and a deploy migration step:** add both on the first deploy.
- **Playwright:** add it once there's a user flow worth protecting.
- **Known gaps:**
  - If `npm run dev` is force-killed, Postgres can keep holding the port. `pkill -f embedded-postgres` clears it.
  - `npm audit` reports 5 high-severity issues, all in dev-only packages from the scaffold.

**Worth learning.**
- **Read the database at request time.** Next 16 turns on Cache Components by default, which pre-builds pages ahead of time. The book list calls `connection()` before its query and sits inside `<Suspense>`. Without that, `next build` would try to run the query and fail in CI.
- **Hooks must be executable.** Git skips a pre-commit hook that isn't executable without any warning. I set the executable bit in git as well as on disk, so a fresh clone gets a hook that actually runs.

turns.sent: Build the first feature: members sign up and sign in, and the organizer creates meetings with a date, a place, and the book.
turns.reply:
Members can now sign up and sign in, and the organizer can schedule meetings with a date and time, a place, and a book. `npm run check` and `npm run build` both pass, and I walked both journeys in Chrome. Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed.** The home page now shows upcoming meetings to signed-in members, soonest first. Signed-out visitors get "Create an account" and "Sign in". The organizer also sees "Schedule a meeting", which opens a form at `/meetings/new`. The organizer types the book's title and author, and if that exact book already exists the meeting reuses it.

Nobody can make themselves organizer from the app. You promote someone with `npm run organizer -- <email>`. Auth uses Better Auth (your usual pick for users in our own Postgres), with sessions in Postgres. Sign-in and sign-up are rate-limited per IP address, and those counts are stored in Postgres too. I removed the old book list from the home page, since it had nothing left to show.

**Evidence.**
- **Tests:** 14 pass against a real throwaway Postgres. They cover:
  - sign-up, the right and wrong password, and a duplicate email (different capitalisation still counts as taken)
  - a 4th sign-in attempt in 10 seconds getting blocked
  - a member being refused when scheduling, with nothing written
  - two meetings saved at the same moment sharing one book
  - past dates and blank fields being rejected
- **Sign-up can't grant organizer:** a sign-up that sends `role: "organizer"` is silently dropped. When I changed `input: false` to `true`, that test failed with "expected 'organizer' to be 'member'".
- **Build:** the first run failed because the build tried to reach the database. `getAuth()` ran before `await headers()`, so the build hit the database while pre-rendering pages. I fixed it in `src/lib/session.ts`.
- **In Chrome, at 375px and 1280px:**
  - I completed sign-up using only the keyboard.
  - A member visiting `/meetings/new` sees "Only the organizer can schedule meetings."
  - A wrong password shows "Invalid email or password" and keeps the email.
  - A past date shows its error next to the field and keeps what was typed.
  - 7:00 PM entered comes back as 7:00 PM.
  - No page scrolls sideways. I fixed one layout bug: "Sign out" was wrapping onto two lines next to a long name.

**Open.**
- **Who can join: unknown.** Anyone who finds the URL can sign up, and every member sees every meeting place, which may be someone's home. Decide open or invite-only before deploying.
- **No password reset or email verification: deferred** until we pick an email provider.
- **Account deletion: deferred.** There's no way for a member to delete their account.
- **Editing meetings: deferred.** Meetings can't be edited or cancelled, and past ones drop off the home page.
- **Deploy settings: deferred.** A deploy needs `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL` and `CLUB_TIME_ZONE`. Without the time zone, meeting times show in UTC on Vercel.

All of these are in PROJECT.md.

**Worth learning.** Better Auth only rate-limits requests that go through its `/api/auth` handler. If sign-in were a server action calling `auth.api.signInEmail()`, the code would look identical and anyone could guess passwords without limit. That's why the auth forms call the client library from the browser.

turns.sent: Next: members suggest books for the next meeting and vote. One vote per member per round.
turns.reply:
Members can now suggest books and vote on the next one, with one vote per member per round. Everything is checked except one thing: I never clicked through it in a browser, because none was reachable from my sandbox.

**How it works.** The organizer clicks "Start a vote" in a new "Pick the next book" section on the home page. While the round is open, any member can suggest a book (title and author) and vote for one suggestion. Voting again moves your vote. Each row shows who suggested it and how many votes it has. Your own vote is highlighted, but nobody sees who voted for what. The organizer closes voting, and everyone sees the ranked results: a winner, a tie ("the organizer picks"), or "no votes". If there's a single winner, the organizer gets a "Schedule a meeting for X" link that opens the meeting form with the title and author filled in.

**How the rules are enforced:**
- **One vote per member per round:** the database allows only one vote row per member per round, so a double-click can't create a second vote.
- **Votes stay in their round:** a vote can't point at a book from a different round.
- **One open round at a time:** two "Start a vote" clicks landing at once still give one round.
- **No late votes:** closing voting waits for any vote or suggestion in progress, so nothing gets in after the round closes.
- **Deleted members:** their votes go, but their suggestions stay, so other members' votes for those books still count.

**Evidence:**
- `npm run check` passes with no lint warnings, 34 tests in total. `npm run build` passes.
- 12 new tests in `tests/votes.test.ts` cover: one vote per member even with two at once, votes replacing each other, refusal after close (the old vote is kept), refusal of a book from an earlier round, members blocked from opening or closing, simultaneous opens, account deletion, and winner/tie/no-votes.
- On the dev server, I signed up two members over HTTP and made one the organizer. Calling "Start a vote" as the member returned "Only the organizer can open or close voting."; as the organizer it opened the round.
- I tried calling the suggest and vote actions directly too, but couldn't get the form data encoded correctly by hand. So I set up suggestions, votes and the close with a throwaway script (since deleted) and checked the rendered HTML:
  - the member's vote shows as pressed, with no close button
  - after closing: "Piranesi by Susanna Clarke won with 2 votes."
  - the schedule link appears only for the organizer
  - the meeting form arrives prefilled
- That check turned up an accessibility bug, now fixed: the vote button's screen-reader label hid the visible "Your vote" text.

**Open** (all recorded in PROJECT.md):
- Nobody has clicked the vote and suggest buttons in a real browser. Walk the flow once in Chrome before merging.
- Ties are left to the organizer: no tie-break rule and no runoff.
- There's no limit on suggestions per member, and suggestions can't be withdrawn.
- "Close voting" has no confirm, and a closed round can't be reopened.
- A member can change their vote but not take it back.
- My test members Ada and Ben (`@example.com`) and one closed round are still in your local dev database. Delete `.data/postgres` if you want a clean slate.

**Worth learning.** The "one open round" rule is a unique index on the constant `(true)` that only covers rows where `closed_at is null`. Every open round gets the same key, so Postgres refuses a second one, and any number of closed rounds is fine. That makes the rule hold even when two requests race, which a "check, then insert" in app code can't do.

turns.sent: Add an email reminder the day before a meeting. There's no email provider yet, so log the emails for now.
turns.reply:
Reminders are built: the day before a meeting, every member who hasn't RSVP'd "no" gets an email saying when, where, and which book. Since there's no email provider yet, the email is printed to the server log. A new route, `/api/cron/reminders`, finds the members who are due and logs one email each. `vercel.json` has Vercel Cron call it once a day, and it refuses any call without the `CRON_SECRET` bearer token. A new `meeting_reminders` table (migration `0004`) records each reminder sent, so a member never gets two for the same meeting, even if the job runs twice or two runs overlap. "Tomorrow" means tomorrow on the club's calendar (`CLUB_TIME_ZONE`), not 24 hours from now. If a daily run is missed, a meeting later the same day still gets its reminder. Nothing is committed yet.

**Assumptions to confirm:**
- **Who gets it:** "maybe" and no-answer members get the reminder; "no" members don't.
- **When it runs:** the cron is set to 16:00 UTC. That's a placeholder until we pick the club's time zone.

**Evidence:**
- **Tests:** `npm run check` passes, 40 tests. The new `tests/reminders.test.ts` covers:
  - a meeting at 6pm Pacific, which is already the next day in UTC
  - meetings two days out and ones that already started (no reminder)
  - "no" members skipped, "maybe" members reminded
  - two overlapping runs plus a rerun, still one email per member
  - a failed send, retried on the next run
- **Against `npm run dev`:** with no secret or a wrong secret the route returned 401. With the secret, the first run returned `{"sent":6,"failed":0}` and printed correct emails to the dev log. The second run returned `{"sent":0}`. I added a test member and meeting to your dev database for this and deleted them afterwards.
- **Build:** `npm run build` succeeds, and the route builds as dynamic, so it never needs a database at build time.

**Still open** (all in PROJECT.md):
- **Personal data in logs:** each logged email contains the member's address and the meeting place. Don't deploy until a real provider replaces the logging.
- **`CRON_SECRET` on deploy:** without it, no reminders go out.
- **At most once:** if the process crashes between recording a reminder and sending it, that member gets no reminder.
- **No unsubscribe** link or setting.
- **Editing meetings:** once meetings can be edited, a changed time won't send a new reminder.

**Worth learning:** there's a choice between recording the reminder before sending it or after. Recording first means a crash at the wrong moment loses one reminder. Recording after means a crash can send it twice. For a book club reminder, a missed email is better than a duplicate. With a real provider, you'd pass it an idempotency key so it drops duplicate sends. That gets you close to exactly once. See the [background jobs guide](https://github.com/devduck123/swe-os/blob/v0.3.0/core/guides/background-jobs-and-webhooks.md).

turns.reply:
**Verdict: the code is in good shape, but it's not ready to share yet.** I fixed two bugs. What's still blocking is deployment and two decisions only you can make.

**What blocks sharing.** These are open items already in PROJECT.md. They aren't new bugs, but "share with the club" means deploying, so they're now in the way:
1. **Anyone can sign up.** Anyone with the URL can create an account and see every meeting place, which may be a home address, plus every member's name. You need to pick open or invite-only (Next item 1). My suggestion is a club invite code checked at sign-up: about 20 lines and no new service. I didn't add it because it's your call and it grows the scope.
2. **Reminder emails would end up in Vercel's logs.** They're only logged right now, so members' email addresses and meeting places would sit in those logs. Pick an email provider, or turn the cron off for the first deploy.
3. **The app isn't deployed.** There's no Neon database, no migration step, and no `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `CLUB_TIME_ZONE` or `CRON_SECRET` set anywhere.

**What I fixed:**
1. **[Medium] `src/lib/auth.ts`: the server accepted any name.** The 100-character limit only existed in the browser form. Sending requests straight to `/api/auth/sign-up/email` with a blank name, a name of just spaces, or a 100,000-character name all returned 200 and saved the account. That name then shows up in everyone's RSVP list ("Coming (3): Ada, , Bob"), on vote suggestions, and in reminder emails. Names are now trimmed and must be 1 to 100 characters, checked in Better Auth's user `databaseHooks`. That covers both sign-up and `update-user`. Four new tests cover it, and I added a Decisions row to PROJECT.md.
2. **[Low] `src/db/reminders.ts`: the reminder subject always said "tomorrow".** If the daily run is missed, the catch-up run sends on the day of the meeting itself, still saying "tomorrow". It now says "today" in that case, and a test checks it.

I also added a test confirming a member can't make themselves organizer through `/api/auth/update-user`. Better Auth already rejects it with a 400, so nothing needed fixing, but the test will catch it if that ever changes.

**What I ran:**
- `npm run check`: 45 tests pass.
- `npm run build`: passes with no database.
- Live check against `npm run dev`:
  - A blank name gets "Enter a name of 1 to 100 characters."
  - A real sign-up lands on the home page signed in.
  - The cron route returns 401 without the secret and 200 with it.
- I deleted the test account I created in your local database afterwards.

Everything else held up: who can do what, RSVPs and votes being one per member, the locking around closing a vote, and reminders not double-sending.

**Optional:** the reminders migration has a name Drizzle made up, `0004_large_madame_web.sql`. Nothing has been committed yet, so now is the cheap time to rename it.

**Not checked:**
- **No browser click-through.** I couldn't click through the pages in a browser, so the vote and suggest buttons still haven't been tested by hand. That's already listed in Gaps.
- **Dev-only dependency warnings remain.** `npm audit` now reports 4 moderate warnings, down from the 5 high that Gaps mentions. They come from drizzle-kit and don't ship with the app.

**Worth learning:** a `maxLength` on an input only limits the form. Better Auth's endpoints are public, so anyone can call them directly and skip the form. Every rule about what gets saved, like `input: false` on `role`, has to be enforced on the server.

reasons.works: Install, test (44 tests) and build all pass on a fresh copy, and sign-up/sign-in, meetings, RSVPs, voting and logged reminders all exist with one-command `npm run dev` on embedded Postgres.
reasons.authorization: Every server action reads the session, organizer checks sit next to the writes in `src/db/meetings.ts` and `src/db/votes.ts`, the user id always comes from the session, and `role` can't be set at sign-up or update; but sign-up is open to anyone with the URL, so a stranger can read members' names and meeting places (possibly home addresses), and the agent flagged this but didn't fix it.
reasons.data_correctness: Composite primary keys plus ON CONFLICT upserts enforce one RSVP and one vote per member, a partial unique index allows only one open round, a composite FK keeps votes inside their round, times are stored as timestamptz, the reminder day is computed in CLUB_TIME_ZONE in SQL, and a claim-row primary key stops duplicate reminders.
reasons.secrets_setup: `.env*` is ignored, `.env.example` is committed with documented empty values, there are no hard-coded secrets apart from local dev defaults, and the cron route uses a timing-safe bearer check; but the README requires installing gitleaks, the migrations 0001–0004 are untracked while the journal that references them is staged, and nothing has been committed.
reasons.tests: Tests run against a real throwaway Postgres and cover concurrent double votes, RSVP replacement, organizer-only actions, refusing role escalation, a meeting at 6pm Pacific that is already the next day in UTC, overlapping reminder runs, and retry after a failed send; the agent also checked that one test fails when its rule is broken.
reasons.simplicity: Scope stayed at meetings, RSVPs, voting and reminders with no extra roles or services, though a gitleaks pre-commit hook plus CI scan, DB-backed rate limiting and a lot of lock/race machinery are a bit heavy for a 12-person club.
reasons.communication: Replies say clearly what was and wasn't verified (no browser click-through for voting, gitleaks hook untested), list open decisions, and give an honest pre-share verdict, though they're dense and occasionally jargon-heavy.
reasons.learning_value: Explanations of why the database constraints beat check-then-insert, why rate limits only apply through the auth handler, the trade-off between at-most-once and at-least-once reminders, and why client-side maxLength isn't validation teach real lessons.

problems.problem: Sign-up is open to anyone who finds the URL, and every signed-in account sees all members' names and every meeting place (possibly a home address); the agent flagged this as blocking but left it unfixed.
Migrations 0001–0004 are untracked while `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` (which references them) is staged, so committing what's staged would produce a repo whose migrations fail on a fresh clone.

The stand-in email sender logs each member's address, name and meeting place to the server log, and `vercel.json` schedules the cron, so the first deploy would put personal data in Vercel logs unless someone disables it.
The meeting time is read in the organizer's browser time zone but displayed and reminded in CLUB_TIME_ZONE, so an organizer whose device is in another zone schedules the wrong instant.
If CLUB_TIME_ZONE is unset it silently falls back to the server's zone (UTC on Vercel), which shifts both the displayed times and the 'day before' reminder window.
The cron is hard-coded to 16:00 UTC as a placeholder, unrelated to the club's zone, so reminders may arrive at an odd local hour.
Voting for a suggestion from another round, or one that doesn't exist, throws VotingClosedError and tells the member 'Voting has closed' while the round is actually open.
The README requires installing gitleaks for the pre-commit hook, and the `prepare` script runs git config, which fails outside a git repo; both are extra friction for a stranger following it.
